messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT PAGER -> SEV2: Multiple serving-runtime pods in eu-west are crashing with CUDA OOMs and immediate restarts. Autoscaler is flapping nodes (scale up -> immediate evict -> scale down). Triggered alerts: pod-restarts, node-drain, increased 5xx rate. Paging oncall.
oncall-sre: I'm on it. jumping in — will collect logs and check autoscaler events. @alex.g can you standby for a possible live handoff? :eyes:
alex.g: here. quick summary? I saw a spike in queued tokens earlier, could be batching + long seqs.
oncall-sre: initial findings: cluster-autoscaler reports rapid add/remove of 4 nodes in last 7min. kube events show pods OOMKilled with message: "OOMKilled: failed to request device memory". /var/log/kern shows cuda driver reset entries.
maya.s: seeing similar in us-west-2 earlier but self-healed. This looks like oscillation causes pods to be rescheduled onto nodes with smaller free GPU mem -> immediate OOM. Also some pods crashloop because they fail to initialize NVidia libraries after driver reset.
zhen: grabbing pod logs for a representative replica: ```
[2026-03-15T10:05:12Z] model_server: allocate_kv_cache failed: CUDA out of memory
[2026-03-15T10:05:12Z] runtime: exit code 137
[2026-03-15T10:05:12Z] traceback: ...
```
zhen: also found repeated liveness probe restarts right after node becomes Ready.
oncall-sre: immediate mitigation options discussed: 1) Temporarily pause cluster autoscaler 2) Drain a single host of low-prio pods and cordon excess nodes 3) Scale down batch size / concurrency for the model route 4) Pin serving to a model variant with lower mem profile. Which to run first?
alex.g: Pause autoscaler first to stop churn. Then cordon troublesome nodes. We should also reduce allowed max surge for rollout to avoid new deploys causing more restarts.
oncall-sre: doing `kubectl annotate cluster-autoscaler redwood.io/paused=true --overwrite` now. Confirming pause applied. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: deploy/rl-model-v3 paused by alex.g for rollout-safety
alex.g: cordoning node eu-west-gpu-7 (most evictions) and draining evicting low-priority batch jobs only: `kubectl cordon eu-west-gpu-7 && kubectl drain eu-west-gpu-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60 --pod-selector='app!=serving'`
ops-jake: heads-up: cordon succeeded, draining finished. freed ~5GB GPU memory on other nodes.
maya.s: temporarily lowering per-route concurrent requests for model: `/routes/rl-model-v3` conf change: `max_concurrency: 2 -> 1` and `batch_window_ms: 40 -> 20`. Pushing config now.
alex.g: neat. also recommending to roll back recent autoscaler config tweak that bumped tolerance to 0.2 — that allowed more aggressive scale-down. @ops-jake can you revert to previous stable config after we stabilise?
ops-jake: can do but will wait until we confirm stability to avoid bouncing.
zhen: note: some pods still show "cuda driver reset" in dmesg. driver version 525.60 patched earlier this month. I suspect a kernel/driver interplay under rapid pod restarts.
lucy.pm: customer impact: multiple customers observed increased 5xx for synth-gen and chat sessions timed out ~500ms extra latency during restarts. Support ticket count increased by 3 in last hour. Updating postmortem stub.
oncall-sre: next actions: 1) keep autoscaler paused for 15m 2) observe pod restart rate and 5xx 3) if stable, slowly unpause and set scale-down cooldown to 10m 4) add temporary placement: avoid scheduling heavy models onto small nodes (nodeSelector tweak)
alex.g: I'll also create a hotfix to the serving runtime to catch out-of-memory at allocation time and fall back to smaller kv_cache allocation and emit a 429 instead of crashloop. Drafting PR now. ETA 30m.
oncall-sre: monitoring: enabling per-model eviction metric stream and tracing. watch window started.
incident-bot: ACTION -> page: escalation to eng-runtime if we see >5 more restarts in 10m window.
ops-jake: restarting nvidia-driver on node eu-west-gpu-3 as driver reset count is high: `systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced` — reboot avoided. Restart finished; kernels show fewer resets.
zhen: after cordon + autoscale pause + config change, pod restarts dropped from 8/min to 0-1/min. 5xx rate trending down.
lucy.pm: communicated to customer success; sent note: "We're seeing autoscaler-induced node churn causing model restarts; we've mitigated and are monitoring. Will follow up with RCA." :email:
alex.g: PR created: `hotfix/oom-fallback-rl-model-v3` link: https://git.redwood/internal/pull/4821
maya.s: can we set a temporary hard qos for the serving pods so they get scheduled with higher eviction protection? might help. (pod priorityClass?)
oncall-sre: set `priorityClassName: high-serving` for rollout; applied to rollout-staging first.
ops-jake: readiness probes modified to have longer initialDelaySeconds so they don't fail immediately after driver resets: `initialDelaySeconds: 25 -> 45`.
incident-bot: NOTE: handoff recommended in 20m to offshift SRE. oncall-sre -> @alex.g taking lead. handoff comment added to incident channel.
alex.g: taking lead. monitoring for next 30m. will coordinate with eng-runtime if anything spikes. thanks everyone.
lucy.pm: logging timeline + customer notes. tagging for postmortem owners: @maya.s @zhen
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, autoscaler paused, cordoned nodes, config adjustments. Severity downgraded to SEV3 pending stable metrics."
